sanskrit: tato 'bravīn mahātejā rāmo lakṣmaṇam agrataḥ sthitaṃ prāggāminaṃ vīraṃ yācamānaṃ kṛtāñjalim
english: Then the great-spirited Rāma spoke to Lakṣmaṇa, who stood before him ready to go forward, a hero entreating with palms joined together.

sanskrit: mayādya saha saumitre tvayi gacchati tad vanam ko bhariṣyati kausalyāṃ sumitrāṃ vā yaśasvinīm
english: "O Saumitri, when you depart with me today into that forest, who will support the illustrious Kausalyā and Sumitrā?"

sanskrit: abhivarṣati kāmair yaḥ parjanyaḥ pṛthivīm iva sa kāmapāśaparyasto mahātejā mahīpatiḥ
english: "The great-spirited king, who showered upon them their desires even as rain-clouds shower upon the earth, is now bound fast in the noose of passion."

sanskrit: sā hi rājyam idaṃ prāpya nṛpasyāśvapateḥ sutā duḥkhitānāṃ sapatnīnāṃ na kariṣyati śobhanam
english: "For she, the daughter of King Aśvapati, having now obtained this kingdom, will not deal kindly with her co-wives who are in distress."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu rāmeṇa lakṣmaṇaḥ ślakṣṇayā girā pratyuvāca tadā rāmaṃ vākyajño vākyakovidam
english: Having been addressed thus by Rāma with gentle words, Lakṣmaṇa — skilled in speech — then replied to that master of eloquence.

sanskrit: tavaiva tejasā vīra bharataḥ pūjayiṣyati kausalyāṃ ca sumitrāṃ ca prayato nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: "By your very glory alone, O hero, Bharata will with devotion honour both Kausalyā and Sumitrā — of this there is no doubt."

sanskrit: kausalyā bibhṛyād āryā sahasram api madvidhān yasyāḥ sahasraṃ grāmāṇāṃ saṃprāptam upajīvanam
english: "The noble Kausalyā could sustain even a thousand men like me, for she has the revenue of a thousand villages to live upon."

sanskrit: dhanur ādāya saśaraṃ khanitrapiṭakādharaḥ agratas te gamiṣyāmi panthānam anudarśayan
english: "Bearing bow and arrows, carrying a spade and a basket, I shall go ahead of you, pointing out the path."

sanskrit: āhariṣyāmi te nityaṃ mūlāni ca phalāni ca vanyāni yāni cānyāni svāhārāṇi tapasvinām
english: "I shall constantly gather for you roots and fruits, and whatever other forest foods are the natural sustenance of ascetics."

sanskrit: bhavāṃs tu saha vaidehyā girisānuṣu raṃsyate ahaṃ sarvaṃ kariṣyāmi jāgrataḥ svapataś ca te
english: "While you take delight with the Vaidehi on mountain slopes, I shall do everything for you, whether you are awake or asleep."

sanskrit: rāmas tv anena vākyena suprītaḥ pratyuvāca tam vrajāpṛcchasva saumitre sarvam eva suhṛjjanam
english: Rāma, greatly pleased by these words, replied to him: "Go take leave, O Saumitri, of all our dear friends."

sanskrit: ye ca rājño dadau divye mahātmā varuṇaḥ svayam janakasya mahāyajñe dhanuṣī raudradarśane
english: "And the two divine bows of fearful aspect which the great-souled Varuṇa himself gave to King Janaka at the great sacrifice —"

sanskrit: abhedyakavace divye tūṇī cākṣayasāyakau ādityavimalau cobhau khaḍgau hemapariṣkṛtau
english: "— the two divine, impenetrable coats of armour, two quivers with inexhaustible arrows, and two swords pure as the sun and adorned with gold —"

sanskrit: satkṛtya nihitaṃ sarvam etad ācāryasadmani sa tvam āyudham ādāya kṣipram āvraja lakṣmaṇa
english: "— all this was reverently deposited in the preceptor's house. Go quickly, Lakṣmaṇa, and bring those weapons here."

sanskrit: sa suhṛjjanam āmantrya vanavāsāya niścitaḥ ikṣvākugurum āmantrya jagrāhāyudham uttamam
english: He, resolute for forest life, took leave of his dear ones and of the preceptor of the Ikṣvāku line, and then took up those supreme weapons.

sanskrit: tad divyaṃ rājaśārdūlaḥ satkṛtaṃ mālyabhūṣitam rāmāya darśayām āsa saumitriḥ sarvam āyudham
english: Saumitri, the tiger among princes, displayed all those divine, duly honoured, garland-adorned weapons to Rāma.

sanskrit: tam uvācātmavān rāmaḥ prītyā lakṣmaṇam āgatam kāle tvam āgataḥ saumya kāṅkṣite mama lakṣmaṇa
english: The self-controlled Rāma, with affection, spoke to Lakṣmaṇa who had arrived: "You have come at the right time, O gentle Lakṣmaṇa, when I was longing for you."

sanskrit: ahaṃ pradātum icchāmi yad idaṃ māmakaṃ dhanam brāhmaṇebhyas tapasvibhyas tvayā saha paraṃtapa
english: "O scorcher of foes, I wish to distribute this wealth of mine — together with you — to the brāhmaṇas and ascetics."

sanskrit: vasantīha dṛḍhaṃ bhaktyā guruṣu dvijasattamāḥ teṣām api ca me bhūyaḥ sarveṣāṃ copajīvinām
english: "The most excellent twice-born who dwell here with steadfast devotion serving the elders — and especially to all who depend on me for their livelihood."

sanskrit: vasiṣṭhaputraṃ tu suyajñam āryaṃ tvam ānayāśu pravaraṃ dvijānām abhiprayāsyāmi vanaṃ samastān abhyarcya śiṣṭān aparān dvijātīn
english: "Quickly bring here the noble Suyajña, son of Vasiṣṭha, foremost among the twice-born; for I shall depart to the forest after honouring all the other venerable brāhmaṇas as well."

sanskrit: tataḥ śāsanam ājñāya bhrātuḥ śubhataraṃ priyam gatvā sa praviveśāśu suyajñasya niveśanam
english: Then, having learned his brother's most auspicious and beloved command, he went quickly and entered the dwelling of Suyajña.

sanskrit: taṃ vipram agnyagārasthaṃ vanditvā lakṣmaṇo 'bravīt sakhe 'bhyāgaccha paśya tvaṃ veśma duṣkarakāriṇaḥ
english: Saluting that brāhmaṇa who was standing by the sacred fire, Lakṣmaṇa said: "Come, dear friend; behold the home of him who performs difficult deeds."

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃdhyām upāsyāśu gatvā saumitriṇā saha juṣṭaṃ tat prāviśal lakṣmyā ramyaṃ rāmaniveśanam
english: Then, after quickly completing the twilight devotions, he went together with Saumitri and entered that charming abode of Rāma, graced with prosperity.

sanskrit: tam āgataṃ vedavidaṃ prāñjaliḥ sītayā saha suyajñam abhicakrāma rāghavo 'gnim ivārcitam
english: With palms joined together, Rāghava, together with Sītā, approached the arrived Suyajña — knower of the Vedas — as one approaches a consecrated fire.

sanskrit: jātarūpamayair mukhyair aṅgadaiḥ kuṇḍalaiḥ śubhaiḥ sahema sūtrair maṇibhiḥ keyūrair valayair api
english: With splendid bracelets and earrings of pure gold, together with golden thread-necklaces, jewels, armlets, and bangles,

sanskrit: anyaiś ca ratnair bahubhiḥ kākutsthaḥ pratyapūjayat suyajñaṃ sa tadovāca rāmaḥ sītāpracoditaḥ
english: — and with many other gems — the Kākutstha honoured Suyajña; and then Rāma, prompted by Sītā, spoke to him.

sanskrit: hāraṃ ca hemasūtraṃ ca bhāryāyai saumya hāraya raśanāṃ cādhunā sītā dātum icchati te sakhe
english: "Convey, O gentle one, this necklace and golden thread to your wife; and now Sītā wishes to give you, dear friend, this girdle as well."

sanskrit: paryaṅkam agryāstaraṇaṃ nānāratnavibhūṣitam tam apīcchati vaidehī pratiṣṭhāpayituṃ tvayi
english: "The Vaidehi also desires to bestow upon you this couch with its excellent coverlet adorned with manifold gems."

sanskrit: nāgaḥ śatruṃ jayo nāma mātulo yaṃ dadau mama taṃ te gajasahasreṇa dadāmi dvijapuṃgava
english: "The elephant named Śatruṃjaya which my maternal uncle gave me — that elephant, worth a thousand common elephants, I give to you, O bull among the twice-born."

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ sa hi rāmeṇa suyajñaḥ pratigṛhya tat rāmalakṣmaṇasītānāṃ prayuyojāśiṣaḥ śivāḥ
english: Thus addressed by Rāma, Suyajña accepted all that and pronounced auspicious blessings upon Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa, and Sītā.

sanskrit: atha bhrātaram avyagraṃ priyaṃ rāmaḥ priyaṃvadaḥ saumitriṃ tam uvācedaṃ brahmeva tridaśeśvaram
english: Then Rāma, sweet of speech, spoke these words to his dear and composed brother Saumitri, even as Brahmā might address Indra, lord of the thirty gods.

sanskrit: agastyaṃ kauśikaṃ caiva tāv ubhau brāhmaṇottamau arcayāhūya saumitre ratnaiḥ sasyam ivāmbubhiḥ
english: "Invite both Agastya and Kauśika, those two most excellent brāhmaṇas, O Saumitri, and honour them with jewels as rain bestows blessings on crops."

sanskrit: kausalyāṃ ca ya āśīrbhir bhaktaḥ paryupatiṣṭhati ācāryas taittirīyāṇām abhirūpaś ca vedavit
english: "And the one who devotedly attends on Kausalyā with blessings — the teacher of the Taittirīyas, handsome and learned in the Vedas —"

sanskrit: tasya yānaṃ ca dāsīś ca saumitre saṃpradāpaya kauśeyāni ca vastrāṇi yāvat tuṣyati sa dvijaḥ
english: "— give to him, O Saumitri, a carriage, female servants, and silk garments — as much as may satisfy that brāhmaṇa."

sanskrit: sūtaś citrarathaś cāryaḥ sacivaḥ suciroṣitaḥ toṣayainaṃ mahārhaiś ca ratnair vastrair dhanais tathā
english: "The noble charioteer Citraratha, a trusted minister of long standing — gratify him too with precious gems, garments, and wealth."

sanskrit: śālivāhasahasraṃ ca dve śate bhadrakāṃs tathā vyañjanārthaṃ ca saumitre gosahasram upākuru
english: "And prepare also, O Saumitri, a thousand loads of fine rice, two hundred auspicious ones, and a thousand cows to be used for relish."

sanskrit: tataḥ sa puruṣavyāghras tad dhanaṃ lakṣmaṇaḥ svayam yathoktaṃ brāhmaṇendrāṇām adadād dhanado yathā
english: Then that tiger among men, Lakṣmaṇa, himself distributed that wealth to the foremost of brāhmaṇas just as instructed, even as Kubera the wealth-giver.

sanskrit: athābravīd bāṣpakalāṃs tiṣṭhataś copajīvinaḥ saṃpradāya bahu dravyam ekaikasyopajīvinaḥ
english: Then, after bestowing abundant goods upon each of his dependants who stood there with tears in their eyes, he spoke to them.

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇasya ca yad veśma gṛhaṃ ca yad idaṃ mama aśūnyaṃ kāryam ekaikaṃ yāvadāgamanaṃ mama
english: "Both Lakṣmaṇa's house and this house of mine are to be kept each one occupied and not left empty, until my return."

sanskrit: ity uktvā duḥkhitaṃ sarvaṃ janaṃ tam upajīvinam uvācedaṃ dhanadhyakṣaṃ dhanam ānīyatām iti tato 'sya dhanam ājahruḥ sarvam evopajīvinaḥ
english: Having spoken thus to all those grieving dependants, he said to the treasurer: "Let the wealth be brought here." Thereupon all his dependants brought all his wealth.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa puruṣavyāghras tad dhanaṃ sahalakṣmaṇaḥ dvijebhyo bālavṛddhebhyaḥ kṛpaṇebhyo 'bhyadāpayat
english: Then that tiger among men, together with Lakṣmaṇa, caused that wealth to be distributed to the twice-born, to children and the aged, and to the destitute.

sanskrit: tatrāsīt piṅgalo gārgyas trijaṭo nāma vai dvijaḥ ā pañcamāyāḥ kakṣyāyā nainaṃ kaś cid avārayat
english: There was among them a tawny-eyed brāhmaṇa of the Gārgya lineage named Trijaṭa; no one barred him up to the fifth enclosure.

sanskrit: sa rājaputram āsādya trijaṭo vākyam abravīt nirdhano bahuputro 'smi rājaputra mahāyaśaḥ uñchavṛttir vane nityaṃ pratyavekṣasva mām iti
english: Approaching the prince, Trijaṭa spoke these words: "O prince of great renown, I am without wealth and have many sons; I live by gleaning grain in the forest — please look after me."

sanskrit: tam uvāca tato rāmaḥ parihāsasamanvitam gavāṃ sahasram apy ekaṃ na tu viśrāṇitaṃ mayā parikṣipasi daṇḍena yāvat tāvad avāpsyasi
english: Then Rāma spoke to him with gentle humour: "Not even one of a thousand cows has yet been distributed by me; however far you throw your staff, that far shall you receive."

sanskrit: sa śāṭīṃ tvaritaḥ kaṭyāṃ saṃbhrāntaḥ pariveṣṭya tām āvidhya daṇḍaṃ cikṣepa sarvaprāṇena vegitaḥ
english: He hastily and excitedly wrapped his cloth tightly round his waist, then whirling his staff hurled it with all the force of his might.

sanskrit: uvāca ca tato rāmas taṃ gārgyam abhisāntvayan manyur na khalu kartavyaḥ parihāso hy ayaṃ mama
english: Then Rāma spoke, reassuring that scion of the Gārgyas: "Do not be angry — for this was but a jest of mine."

sanskrit: tataḥ sabhāryas trijaṭo mahāmunir gavām anīkaṃ pratigṛhya moditaḥ yaśobalaprītisukhopabṛṃhiṇīs tad āśiṣaḥ pratyavadan mahātmanaḥ
english: Then the great sage Trijaṭa, together with his wife, joyfully received the herd of cattle and in return offered to the great-souled one blessings that swelled with fame, strength, joy, and happiness.

sanskrit: dattvā tu saha vaidehyā brāhmaṇebhyo dhanaṃ bahu jagmatuḥ pitaraṃ draṣṭuṃ sītayā saha rāghavau
english: Having distributed abundant wealth to the brāhmaṇas together with the Vaidehi, the two Rāghavas set out together with Sītā to see their father.

sanskrit: tato gṛhīte duṣprekṣye aśobhetāṃ tadāyudhe mālādāmabhir āsakte sītayā samalaṃkṛte
english: Then, with those terrible-to-behold weapons taken up and adorned by Sītā with garlands and strings of flowers, the two shone resplendent.

sanskrit: tataḥ prāsādaharmyāṇi vimānaśikharāṇi ca adhiruhya janaḥ śrīmān udāsīno vyalokayat
english: Then the prosperous people, climbing the palaces, mansions, and the pinnacles of towers, looked on with sorrowful detachment.

sanskrit: na hi rathyāḥ sma śakyante gantuṃ bahujanākulāḥ āruhya tasmāt prāsādān dīnāḥ paśyanti rāghavam
english: For the streets thronged with so many people that it was impossible to pass through them; hence they climbed the palaces and in grief watched Rāghava.

sanskrit: padātiṃ varjitacchatraṃ rāmaṃ dṛṣṭvā tadā janāḥ ūcur bahuvidhā vācaḥ śokopahatacetasaḥ
english: Seeing Rāma proceeding on foot without his royal umbrella, the people, their hearts stricken with grief, uttered many diverse words.

sanskrit: yaṃ yāntam anuyāti sma caturaṅgabalaṃ mahat tam ekaṃ sītayā sārdham anuyāti sma lakṣmaṇaḥ
english: "He whom a great four-division army used to follow when he went forth — now only Lakṣmaṇa follows that one alone, together with Sītā."

sanskrit: aiśvaryasya rasajñaḥ san kāmināṃ caiva kāmadaḥ necchaty evānṛtaṃ kartuṃ pitaraṃ dharmagauravāt
english: "He who knows the taste of sovereignty and who is the fulfiller of desires for those who desire, yet he does not wish to render his father's word false, out of reverence for dharma."

sanskrit: yā na śakyā purā draṣṭuṃ bhūtair ākāśagair api tām adya sītāṃ paśyanti rājamārgagatā janāḥ
english: "Sītā, who could not be seen even by beings moving through the sky, is today seen by the people who have come into the royal road."

sanskrit: aṅgarāgocitāṃ sītāṃ raktacandana sevinīm varṣam uṣṇaṃ ca śītaṃ ca neṣyaty āśu vivarṇatām
english: "Sītā, accustomed to body-unguents and to the use of red sandalwood paste, will quickly be discoloured by rain, heat, and cold."

sanskrit: adya nūnaṃ daśarathaḥ sattvam āviśya bhāṣate na hi rājā priyaṃ putraṃ vivāsayitum arhati
english: "Surely today Daśaratha speaks under the sway of some other force — for a king ought not to banish a beloved son."

sanskrit: nirguṇasyāpi putrasyā kāthaṃ syād vipravāsanam kiṃ punar yasya loko 'yaṃ jito vṛttena kevalam
english: "How could there be banishment even of a son without virtues? — and how much more of him who has won the entire world by his conduct alone?"

sanskrit: ānṛśaṃsyam anukrośaḥ śrutaṃ śīlaṃ damaḥ śamaḥ rāghavaṃ śobhayanty ete ṣaḍguṇāḥ puruṣottamam
english: "Non-cruelty, compassion, learning, good character, self-control, and tranquillity — these six virtues adorn Rāghava, the most excellent of men."

sanskrit: tasmāt tasyopaghātena prajāḥ paramapīḍitāḥ audakānīva sattvāni grīṣme salilasaṃkṣayāt
english: "Therefore, by the affliction done to him, the subjects are sorely tormented, like water-creatures in summer when the waters dry up."

sanskrit: pīḍayā pīḍitaṃ sarvaṃ jagad asya jagatpateḥ mūlasyevopaghātena vṛkṣaḥ puṣpaphalopagaḥ
english: "The entire world is afflicted by the affliction of this lord of the world, just as a fruit- and flower-bearing tree is afflicted by the striking of its root."

sanskrit: te lakṣmaṇa iva kṣipraṃ sapatnyaḥ sahabāndhavāḥ gacchantam anugacchāmo yena gacchati rāghavaḥ
english: "Let us quickly follow, together with our kin, even as Lakṣmaṇa does — following where Rāghava goes."

sanskrit: udyānāni parityajya kṣetrāṇi ca gṛhāṇi ca ekaduḥkhasukhā rāmam anugacchāma dhārmikam
english: "Abandoning our gardens, our fields, and our houses, sharing in one sorrow and one joy, let us follow the righteous Rāma."

sanskrit: samuddhṛtanidhānāni paridhvastājirāṇi ca upāttadhanadhānyāni hṛtasārāṇi sarvaśaḥ
english: "Our treasuries dug up and emptied, our courtyards ruined, our grain and wealth taken, stripped of all substance —"

sanskrit: rajasābhyavakīrṇāni parityaktāni daivataiḥ asmattyaktāni veśmāni kaikeyī pratipadyatām
english: "— our houses covered with dust, abandoned by the gods, deserted by us — let Kaikeyī have them."

sanskrit: vanaṃ nagaram evāstu yena gacchati rāghavaḥ asmābhiś ca parityaktaṃ puraṃ saṃpadyatāṃ vanam
english: "Let the forest where Rāghava goes become the city; and let this city, abandoned by us, become a forest."

sanskrit: bilāni daṃṣṭriṇaḥ sarve sānūni mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ asmattyaktaṃ prapadyantāṃ sevyamānaṃ tyajantu ca
english: "Let all the fanged beasts take to the lairs and the mountain slopes to the deer and birds; and what we abandon — let them inhabit what was frequented, and abandon what was abandoned."

sanskrit: ity evaṃ vividhā vāco nānājanasamīritāḥ śuśrāva rāmaḥ śrutvā ca na vicakre 'sya mānasaṃ
english: Rāma heard all these diverse words uttered by people of every kind; and having heard them, his mind was not shaken.

sanskrit: pratīkṣamāṇo 'bhijanaṃ tadārtam anārtarūpaḥ prahasann ivātha jagāma rāmaḥ pitaraṃ didṛkṣuḥ pitur nideśaṃ vidhivac cikīrṣuḥ
english: Waiting for those kinsfolk who were suffering, yet himself appearing without distress and almost smiling, Rāma went forward, wishing to see his father and to fulfil his father's command in due order.

sanskrit: tat pūrvam aikṣvākasuto mahātmā rāmo gamiṣyan vanam ārtarūpam vyatiṣṭhata prekṣya tadā sumantraṃ pitur mahātmā pratihāraṇārtham
english: Before that, the great-souled son of the Ikṣvāku line, Rāma, about to depart for the forest, paused on seeing Sumantra there, intending to use him as an intermediary to his father.

sanskrit: pitur nideśena tu dharmavatsalo vanapraveśe kṛtabuddhiniścayaḥ sa rāghavaḥ prekṣya sumantram abravīn nivedayasvāgamanaṃ nṛpāya me
english: The Rāghava, devoted to dharma and with his resolve firmly fixed on entering the forest in accordance with his father's command, looked at Sumantra and said: "Announce my arrival to the king."
